title: Erdos #1148: Representation as x^2 + y^2 - z^2

problemStatement.formal: Is every sufficiently large n representable as x^2 + y^2 - z^2 with x^2 <= n, y^2 <= n, and z^2 <= n?
problemStatement.plain: Can every large integer be written as a difference of three bounded squares, with all three squares no larger than the target integer?
whyMatters: Turns a simple-looking representation question into a constrained sums-of-two-squares problem.
The strict bound x^2, y^2, z^2 <= n blocks the obvious odd-number difference-of-squares identity.
The finite search space gives good Lean infrastructure for verified examples without settling the open conjecture.

proven: Lean defines Representation, IsRepresentable, and IsRepresentableWith using x^2 + y^2 = z^2 + n to avoid natural-number subtraction pitfalls.
The file proves perfect-square representability, many small positive examples, and individual non-representability results for 3, 6, 11, and 15.
It proves component bounds, a finite nonRepresentable set up to N, sum-of-two-squares reformulations, and representation constructors such as swap and shifted sums.
open: The eventual representability conjecture is the single active axiom erdos_1148.
The comment that 6563 is the largest known exception is not a Lean theorem.
The listed small negative examples are individual theorems, not a complete classified range.
knownResults.goal: Use the verified representation infrastructure and examples while keeping the global sufficiency conjecture marked as open and axiomatized.

currentState.focus: Metadata now reflects the rich representation scaffold, small verified examples, and the one axiomatized global conjecture.
blockers: Eventual representability for all sufficiently large n remains open in Lean.
The largest-known-exception statement is documentation only.
currentState.nextAction: A natural next proof slice is to connect the Boolean checker or sum-of-two-squares reformulation to larger verified ranges.
